question: The seventh paragraph indicates that what strikes Ines about the half second is that:

options.A: it contradicts what she was taught about tying up in August.
options.B: it asks so much less of her than the winter she had braced for.
options.C: she has not been told which landings require it and which do not.
options.D: it is a knack she believes only someone with Bell's years could have.

question: Which discovery would most strongly support the author's claim that a printed page is a misleading witness to the punchcutter's letter?

options.A: a nineteenth-century revival that traced the same page the Sarto foundry used
options.B: a second copy of the same book, inked more lightly throughout
options.C: a contract showing that the punchcutter was paid by the size rather than by the font, at a rate fixed before he began
options.D: a surviving set of punches whose filed forms are markedly sharper than the pages they printed

question: A visitor reports a dry upper gallery with no stream that is wholly dark on entry, shines for two minutes after her lamp is switched off, and shows the light as a single sheet along one layer of flowstone. This report:

options.A: fits both accounts equally, since neither excludes a dry gallery.
options.B: favours Passage A, because the light is steady rather than flickering.
options.C: favours Passage B on each of the marks the two passages use to tell the explanations apart.
options.D: favours Passage A, because the light comes back after a disturbance.

question: Which of the following findings, if reported by a later study of Sang-hwa Street, would most undermine the author's explanation of why the vendors' rules are obeyed?

options.A: Most vendors expect to leave the market within a year and follow the rules anyway.
options.B: The queue for a pitch had shortened from six years to four.
options.C: Most vendors could not name a single member of the Wednesday board or say when it had last met.
options.D: Most vendors sell items unrelated to those of their immediate neighbours.
